complexity.correctness_reason: Crashes with AttributeError on lists[j].val when the array contains an empty list, e.g. lists = [[]] (heads arrive as None) — an input the statement explicitly permits (Example 3); the code never filters out None heads before dereferencing them.
complexity.notes: The early break on lists[j].val == prev.val is sound because the merged sequence is non-decreasing, so any head equal to prev.val is a global minimum of the remaining values. The dummy node's value is never relied upon for ordering, so the -10000 literal is harmless. List/Optional are used without a typing import, which works on LeetCode/NeetCode's harness but not in bare Python. The vals bookkeeping from the previous version (which was dead state) has been removed.
complexity.summary: Repeatedly scans all k list heads to find the minimum-valued head (with an early break when a head equals the previously merged value, which is provably a valid minimum) and appends that node to the result, dropping exhausted lists. This is the naive O(n*k) selection-merge rather than a heap or divide-and-conquer merge.
